original_card.claim_under_review: Test whether fixed recent joint support distinguishes observations beyond axis-aligned bounds; do not assume a breakout predicts direction.

status_record.status: NOT_TESTED: joint-support estimator absent; compare fixed joint support with axis-aligned bounds on fit.

basis.review_scope: Design only. No production arrays, target values, models, remote actions, or fits were read or run.

frozen_design_assumptions.panel: Existing R3 exposed fit panel only: 64 fit components; no evaluation components or score/grade use.

coordinates.label_source: canonical data.py metadata as reported by the task owner
coordinates.qualification: The labels do not establish common physical units or economic meaning across i0/i1. Interpret the pair only as these two fixed coordinates unless source documentation proves more.

frozen_design_assumptions.queries: Original stride-40 eligible rows, with t >= 256; each query uses only the same sequence's strict-past window [t-256,t).
classes: outside the closed axis-aligned window box (range extension)
inside the closed box but outside the closed convex hull (joint-only novelty)
frozen_design_assumptions.target_access: Target-free. Do not read target values; no target-conditioned moments, evaluation, training, or quality grade. Only the fixed x inputs and the existing row/sequence masks, mappings, and source hashes needed to define eligible queries are in scope.

review.decision_value: Useful as a cheap falsifier for this one coordinate pair and one window: if the joint-only class is absent or concentrated in a small number of components/one fixed half, a broader hull implementation is not justified by this screen. A repeatable nontrivial class only shows that the hull differs geometrically from marginal bounds; it does not show predictive value.
required_controls: Treat the convex hull as a subset of its axis-aligned bounding box and report all three mutually exclusive classes, not only the primary joint-only class.

Include hull degeneracies (one point, collinear/segment, and duplicate points) and define closed-boundary inclusion and orientation handling before execution; do not tune a numerical tolerance from outcomes.

Report counts and rates per component plus equal-component-weight summaries and the two pre-fixed 32-component halves. Rows within a component are serially dependent; halves are stability checks, not independent inferential replicates.
Freeze the component-to-half assignment, coordinate IDs, eligibility/mask handling, and query count before looking at results. Keep the physical-unit caveat attached to every interpretation.
falsifiers: The joint-only category appears in only one fixed half or is dominated by a few components, indicating weak panel-wide stability.
Most departures are outside the box, while the joint-only category is negligible; marginal range extension then explains nearly all observed novelty for this fixed pair/window.
limits: This is a current-point-versus-past-window geometry screen, not a matched test of the same current state under different histories.

Regime drift, local dependence, and the current point's location can create the joint-only category; its occurrence does not establish information about future labels or an incremental forecast benefit.
One pair and W=256 do not establish the full state-geometry mechanism or robustness to coordinate/window choice. No post-result coordinate/window search is authorized by this review.
review.advance_rule: For a descriptive screen, report the fixed counts/rates and component distribution without significance claims. If a binary go/no-go threshold is desired, set its numerical prevalence and component-coverage threshold before inspecting outputs; this review does not invent a post-hoc threshold.

resource_note: The proposed 2D, 256-point rolling hull over fixed stride rows is plausibly bounded, but the implementation owner must establish the exact eligible-query bound and CPU/memory estimate from metadata before execution. No production-data access was part of this review.
